newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end off despite quarter-end dressing.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end off despite quarter-end dressing.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly lower on Monday, reversing earlier gains boosted by end-of-quarter window dressing by institutional investors, brokers said.
The index ended 3.49 points or 0.05 percent lower at 6,504.68. Turnover was a modest T$32.23 billion.
Brokers noted caution after margin loans outstanding reached a three-month-high at T$216 billion on Thursday.
"Investors are worried that such a high rate of margin loans outstanding might trigger selling pressure in the near future," said Oliver Fang of National Securities.
Plastics and machinery shares fell most, followed by constructions and electronics.

But financials rose slightly, with state-run Chiao Tung Bank up by the daily seven percent limit to T$66.5, its third consecutive limit up since its debut last Wednesday. The market was closed for holidays on Friday and Saturday.
Paper, steel and cement shares also firmed. Taiwan Pulp rose 60 cents to T$22.3 and China Steel gained 10 cents to T$25.6.
Several brokers said they expected a firming trend in the fourth quarter and the first quarter of 1997.
"Many people expect the index to test high around 7,000 points in the fourth quarter and the first quarter of next year," Fang said.
Brokers said they also expected the index to test the year's closing high of 6,624 points this week due to positive sentiment among both local and foreign institutional investors.
"However," Fang said, "buying will turn cautious (with the index) nearing 6,600 as domestic economic fundamentals have not shown apparent recovery so far."
A 6,450-6,550 range was seen for Tuesday.
